text: The AI output indicating glioma is indeterminate and should be regarded as inconclusive; it does not constitute a diagnosis and must not be used to guide treatment. Glioma is a broad term for tumours arising from glial cells, and the group spans a wide range of biological behaviour, so the label alone is not a complete clinical description [nci-cns-pdq-hp] [who-cns5]. The system assigns only a broad tumour category from image data and cannot determine grade, molecular subtype, margins or volume, and an imaging appearance suggestive of glioma does not establish grade, which is the dominant driver of prognosis [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. In the project's own evaluation glioma was the weakest class for recall, remaining the least reliable of the four tumour categories [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. Consequently the result requires review by a qualified radiologist and the multidisciplinary neuro-oncology team, with clinical correlation and discussion of any neurological red-flag symptoms with a specialist physician [nci-cns-pdq-hp] [ninds-brain-tumors] [ninds-brain-tumors]. The tool holds no CDSCO registration and is not a medical device, and its use must comply with ethical guidelines that require validation before patient care [cdsco-md-rules] [neurasight-system] [icmr-ai-ethics]. Until a qualified professional has examined the imaging and clinical context, the finding must not be acted upon.
